summary: Rework of task 26.3 (attempt 2) resolving exactly the three findings of docs/implementation/26.3/test-quality-review.json. In this attempt, only scripts/check-agents.sh and the from-phase-26 Enforcement scope sentence of docs/agent-contracts.md changed, plus this report (docs/plan/README.md still carries the accepted attempt-1 edit and was not touched). TQ-01: the pre-change all-phases rule is restored as its own guard section ('plan state lists the reviewer report from every phase'): any task with a worker-report.json and no exemption must list a reviewer-report entry in docs/plan/state.json reports; the restored check is not gated by APPLIES_FROM_PHASE, so de-listing a historical reviewer report below phase 20 fails again, while the stronger from-phase-20 on-disk evidence section (base report for every kind on disk plus every on-disk attempt for every listed kind) is unchanged and runs independently — both emit their own err lines. TQ-02: role_mix is now recomputed over all recorded invocations — the task-record invocations plus the phase record's own phase-reviewer entries — so it sums to subagent_invocations_total and matches the phase-20 worked example (phase-reviewer: 2); the guard comment states that basis and the contract bullet now reads 'sums recomputed from all recorded invocations (task-level plus the phase record's own)'. TQ-03: from phase 26, when a phase directory contains a phase-review*.json, the orchestration record's subagents must contain at least one phase-reviewer entry and aggregate.phase_reviewer_invocations must equal the count of those entries; otherwise the guard fails. Phases 20-25 remain grandfathered by AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE=26. Probes: de-listing 15.1 fails again with the pre-change script's exact line; a fabricated unlisted 20.1 attempt and base kind both fail and pass when listed; lowering AGGREGATE_APPLIES_FROM_PHASE to 20 makes phase 20 reconcile fully including role_mix while phase 21 still reconciles; a phase-26-format conforming record passes while an omitted phase-reviewer entry and a task-record-only role_mix both fail. On the real tree, scripts/check-agents.sh currently fails only the disclosed in-progress 26.3 gate lines (12 of 15 sections report ok, 3 fail); on the clean copy with docs/implementation/26.3 set aside it exits 0 with all 15 sections ok, and scripts/check-docs.sh exits 0 with all nine sections ok there.
validation: bash -n scripts/check-agents.sh -> no output, exit 0 (syntax ok).

The three failures are exactly the disclosed in-progress 26.3 transient and nothing else: 'FAIL: task 26.3 has a worker report but no reviewer report (add an exemption only if covered)'; 'FAIL: task 26.3 has a reviewer report on disk but docs/plan/state.json does not list it in reports' (the restored all-phases check); 'FAIL: task 26.3 has on-disk report evidence not listed in docs/plan/state.json reports: docs/implementation/26.3/worker-report.json, docs/implementation/26.3/test-quality-review.json'. Then 'check-agents: FAIL'. All other sections report ok, including 'ok: plan state lists the on-disk report evidence', 'ok: contract aggregate enforcement scope agrees with the script' and 'ok: phase aggregates reconcile with the task records'.

Real tree: (source /config/arrtags-env.sh; bash scripts/check-docs.sh) -> exit 1; sections 1-8 all ok including 'ok: doc budget checked', section 9 'agent report contracts conform' fails and mirrors the same three check-agents lines; 'check-docs: FAIL'. interpretations.question: What exactly is 'all invocations in the phase record's subagents array' for the role_mix recomputation?
interpretations.chosen: The union of the task-record invocations and the phase record's own phase-reviewer entries ($inv + $pr), not a raw read of $o.subagents.
interpretations.basis: The delegation's parenthetical '(task-level plus phase-reviewer entries)' and its requirement that role_mix 'sums to subagent_invocations_total', which is itself defined as task_level_invocations + phase_reviewer_invocations. Both in-repo precedents reconcile under the union: phase 20 (13 = 11 + 2) and phase 21 (56 = 56 + 0).
interpretations.impact: A phase record whose copied task-level entries diverge from the task records is not detected by role_mix, because role_mix stays derived from the same task-record authority as the other task-level fields. Phase-reviewer entries are now included, matching the phase-20 worked example.

interpretations.question: Should the contract's from-phase-26 bullet also state the phase-reviewer requirement that TQ-03 adds to the guard, or only the recomputation basis the delegation named?
interpretations.chosen: State both in the same bullet: recomputation basis over all recorded invocations, and a required phase-reviewer invocation whenever phase-review*.json exists.
interpretations.basis: docs/agent-contracts.md is the single source of truth for the rules scripts/check-agents.sh enforces; a guard that rejects a contract-conforming record would be the same class of contract/enforcement mismatch TQ-01 fixed. The clause fits the A5 bullet and the file remains at the 220-line budget.
interpretations.impact: A phase-26+ record with a phase-review file that omits the phase-reviewer invocation is now contract-nonconforming as well as guard-rejected; phases before 26 remain exempt.

interpretations.question: Keep the pre-change error wording for the restored all-phases check?
interpretations.chosen: Yes, verbatim: 'task $b has a reviewer report on disk but $state does not list it in reports'.
interpretations.basis: Faithful restoration makes the probe byte-comparable with the pre-change script (the test-quality audit quoted this exact line), and the delegation asked to restore the requirement, not to rewrite its message.
interpretations.impact: For a task whose reviewer file is absent (for example the in-progress 26.3), the message mentions a file that is not on disk; the preceding pairing section separately reports the missing file. Behaviour is identical to the pre-change script.

interpretations.question: The TQ-03 equality requirement is already covered by the aggregate recomputation's phase_reviewer_invocations comparison; keep a second explicit err line?
interpretations.chosen: Yes: when a phase-review file exists and aggregate.phase_reviewer_invocations differs from the record's phase-reviewer entry count, the new check emits its own err in addition to the aggregate mismatch line.
interpretations.basis: The delegation states the equality as part of the TQ-03 fix; the explicit line makes the phase-review accounting failure legible even inside a long aggregate mismatch list.
interpretations.impact: A wrong phase_reviewer_invocations can produce two FAIL lines instead of one; there is no false-pass direction.

known_limitations: Exact behaviour after this report is persisted: docs/implementation/26.3/ contains worker-report.json, test-quality-review.json and worker-report.attempt-2.json; reviewer-report.json does not exist and docs/plan/state.json lists no 26.3 reports. In that state bash scripts/check-agents.sh exits 1 with exactly three 'FAIL:' lines and then 'check-agents: FAIL': 'FAIL: task 26.3 has a worker report but no reviewer report (add an exemption only if covered)', 'FAIL: task 26.3 has a reviewer report on disk but docs/plan/state.json does not list it in reports', 'FAIL: task 26.3 has on-disk report evidence not listed in docs/plan/state.json reports: docs/implementation/26.3/worker-report.json, docs/implementation/26.3/test-quality-review.json' (worker-report.attempt-2.json is not required while the task lists no report kinds, per contract rule 5). 12 of 15 sections report ok, the 3 failing sections are the pairing, all-phases listing and on-disk evidence checks; scripts/check-docs.sh mirrors this in section 9 while its other eight sections are ok. Precondition: the orchestrator has not yet completed the 26.3 implementation review and listed the reports. Consequence: the authoritative PASS runs in validation are on the clean copy with docs/implementation/26.3 set aside; the interim real-tree failure clears when the orchestrator writes docs/implementation/26.3/reviewer-report.json and lists worker-report.json, reviewer-report.json, test-quality-review.json and worker-report.attempt-2.json in docs/plan/state.json reports (listing worker-report.json also makes its preserved .attempt-2.json required).

Phase 26 has no orchestration record on disk yet, so the guard's phase-26 aggregate branch is a no-op on the shipped tree. The TQ-02 and TQ-03 conformance evidence is a fabricated phase-26 record built from the on-disk 26.1/26.2 task records plus one synthetic phase-reviewer entry; the record that will actually ship is expected to cover more tasks and will be exercised for the first time at the phase gate. A wrong convention chosen then fails loudly, it cannot pass silently.

The TQ-03 check keys on the filename glob phase-review*.json and runs only when a phase >= 26 has an orchestration record. A phase-review*.json with no orchestration record is not cross-checked by the aggregate section (the contract's aggregate rule is keyed to records), and a record with at least one phase-reviewer entry whose aggregate counts match cannot be shown to enumerate every phase-review invocation that occurred; the guard enforces presence, equality and per-entry sums, not completeness of the set.

The restored all-phases check keeps the pre-change message 'has a reviewer report on disk', which reads imprecisely when the reviewer file is absent (the in-progress 26.3 case); the preceding pairing check reports the missing file separately. This wording is unchanged from the pre-change script by design (probe a shows byte-identical output).
